evidence: Supplied manual forms and packed-field tables plus authored offline calendar tests; no host/controller clock writes

sources.topic: GET_TIME INTEGER output and year/month/day/hour/minute/two-second fields
SET_TIME INTEGER input, zero no-op and conflicting table/detail field ranges

implemented.service: Explicit CalendarClock(datetime or packed INTEGER), frozen by default; ExecutionContext.calendar shares it across programs and linked routines
implemented.get: Checked ordinary INTEGER output, shared packed conversion helpers and complete calendar validation before writing
implemented.set: Changes only the supplied clock anchor; zero does not sample or change it; invalid input or adapter preserves existing state
implemented.elapsed: Optional explicit synchronous nonnegative integer microsecond adapter; constructor anchor sample, backward-observation guard, fractional carry and calendar range checks
implemented.persistence: Complete naive ISO datetime with microseconds; callbacks and elapsed origin omitted; restore is frozen
implemented.ownership: Exact output type, source-order capture, FOR guards, prior effects, frame cleanup and value-free service records

portable_choices: Use GET_TIME table layout also used by text conversions, resolving SET_TIME detail/table conflict explicitly
Years 1980..2107, signed 32-bit patterns, floor odd seconds when packed; internal microseconds retained
No implicit host-date sampling or default calendar; SET_TIME(0) also requires the explicit service
Adapter constructor sampling establishes elapsed origin; callbacks never set the operating-system clock
Setting calendar time does not alter connected timers, scheduler time or microsecond counters
remaining: Native invalid-date/timing equivalence, timezone and locale conversion, physical controller acquisition/configuration and strict mode
